title: Choosing IntelliJ as the project-standard IDE
answer: For this project I use IntelliJ IDEA. I am aware that Java development can also be done in Eclipse or other IDEs, but AeroTopo standardizes the learning and development workflow on IntelliJ. It gives me strong Java code intelligence, project/JDK configuration, Maven integration, Spring-aware tooling, Git support, terminal access, debugging, refactoring, and test execution in one environment. The build itself remains Maven-based, so the project is not technically dependent on IntelliJ; IntelliJ is the IDE I use for the day-to-day workflow.

steps.title: Use the project-standard IDE
steps.question: A single project-standard IDE makes navigation, screenshots, shortcuts, and simulator actions consistent while Maven keeps the underlying build portable. A team benefits when its documented learning workflow uses one predictable IDE even though Java itself is IDE-independent. Why is AeroTopo standardized on IntelliJ for these lessons?
steps.why: A single project-standard IDE makes navigation, screenshots, shortcuts, and simulator actions consistent while Maven keeps the underlying build portable.
steps.why_te: AeroTopo project ni IntelliJ lo open chesi start cheddam. Same IDE use chesthe navigation and shortcuts consistent ga untayi. Maven build IntelliJ bayata kuda run avvachu.

steps.title: Open IntelliJ settings
steps.question: IDE settings control behavior such as plugins, editor preferences, keymaps, inspections, and other developer-facing configuration. Choosing an IDE includes configuring its own development environment. Why is the Settings surface part of evaluating IntelliJ as the project-standard tool? The Open IntelliJ settings action exposes the relevant IntelliJ state directly, so the question stays tied to observable project behavior rather than generic interview wording.
steps.why: IDE settings control behavior such as plugins, editor preferences, keymaps, inspections, and other developer-facing configuration.
steps.why_te: IntelliJ Settings lo ee option ni check cheddam. IntelliJ Settings lo plugins, editor preferences, keymaps, inspections lanti developer configuration untundi. IDE choice lo ee environment kuda important.

steps.title: Verify project-level Java configuration
steps.question: Explicit Project SDK and language-level settings align IntelliJ with the repository's intended Java baseline instead of relying on whatever is installed locally. Java is portable across IDEs, so what prevents an IntelliJ project from becoming dependent on arbitrary local defaults?
steps.why: Explicit Project SDK and language-level settings align IntelliJ with the repository's intended Java baseline instead of relying on whatever is installed locally.
steps.why_te: Project SDK ikkada kanipistundi. AeroTopo Java 21 use chestunda ani easy ga check cheyyachu. IntelliJ wrong JDK use chesthe compile errors leda wrong language features kanipinchachu.

steps.title: Verify Maven remains the build authority
steps.question: Maven lets the same project compile and test from the terminal and CI, which keeps IDE choice separate from build reproducibility. If the project standardizes on IntelliJ, why should Maven still remain the authoritative build model rather than IDE-only build metadata?
steps.why: Maven lets the same project compile and test from the terminal and CI, which keeps IDE choice separate from build reproducibility.
steps.why_te: Maven window lo dependencies, plugins and lifecycle goals kanipistayi. Project ela build avutundo ikkada easy ga check cheyyachu. Same Maven setup local machine and CI lo use avutundi.

steps.title: Use IntelliJ's Spring awareness
steps.question: Spring-aware tooling can surface framework concepts such as beans and mappings that a plain text editor cannot infer as directly. What makes an IDE especially useful for Spring Boot beyond basic Java syntax highlighting? The Use IntelliJ's Spring awareness action exposes the relevant IntelliJ state directly, so the question stays tied to observable project behavior rather than generic interview wording.
steps.why: Spring-aware tooling can surface framework concepts such as beans and mappings that a plain text editor cannot infer as directly.
steps.why_te: Spring view lo project beans kanipistayi. Java class Spring manage chestunna object ga runtime lo load ayinda ani ikkada check cheyyachu. Project grow ayina appudu bean ekkada undi ani find cheyyadaniki ee view useful.

steps.title: Keep version control integrated
steps.question: A useful IDE keeps diffs, branches, changes, and history close to the source without changing the fact that Git remains the underlying version-control system. Why is source-control integration relevant when choosing a daily IDE for a collaborative Java project?
steps.why: A useful IDE keeps diffs, branches, changes, and history close to the source without changing the fact that Git remains the underlying version-control system.
steps.why_te: Git window lo changed files and current branch kanipistayi. Code lo em marchamo commit mundu ikkada check cheyyachu. Wrong change unte diff chusi easy ga identify cheyyachu.

steps.title: Keep direct CLI access available
steps.question: Direct CLI access proves the project is not dependent on hidden IDE behavior and makes troubleshooting closer to CI and production workflows. If IntelliJ is the chosen IDE, why should the workflow still make Java and Maven commands available through an integrated terminal?
steps.why: Direct CLI access proves the project is not dependent on hidden IDE behavior and makes troubleshooting closer to CI and production workflows.
steps.why_te: IntelliJ terminal ni open chesi commands run cheddam. Direct CLI access valla project hidden IDE behavior meeda depend kaadani prove avutundi. Troubleshooting kuda CI mariyu production workflow ki daggara ga untundi.

steps.title: Validate the standardized IDE workflow
steps.question: Running the Maven tests from the project confirms that IntelliJ and the portable build model work together correctly. What final check shows that choosing IntelliJ as the standard IDE has not broken the portable Maven-based project workflow? The Maven goal `test` verifies the idea through the project's reproducible build lifecycle instead of relying on editor state alone.
steps.why: Running the Maven tests from the project confirms that IntelliJ and the portable build model work together correctly.
steps.why_te: Maven tests pass ayithe IntelliJ use chestunna kuda project build Maven dwara correct ga run avutundi ani confirm avutundi.
